doc.title: Ruth Brisbane interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 2, 2013

title: Blues form and the vocal coach her sister-in-law arranged
summary: Standard blues form; her sister-in-law sent her to a blues and R&B vocal coach.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the blues is, and why every jazz player needs it

blocks.x: So for you, when she said, “You need to sing some blues” was part of that the blues song with the three lines, the first two being the same, and was that part of the definition of a blues or was it more about feel?
No, I believe the standard blues, yes. Standard blues.
And so who did she direct you to, to be a blues model?

Who did she direct me to. She really did not direct me to any model, but I had a sister-in- law who was divorced from my brother but she took an interest in my singing. And she sent me to a vocal coach. And he was mainly blues and R&B, and mainly gave me songs that he had written. So still, getting the standard blues, I had to work on getting that myself.
